clauses.reason: Section 1 as signed designated the Director of the Office of Management and Budget for two authorities, section 5 joint funding regulations and section 500(a) transfer of unexpended appropriations. Executive Order 11784 section 2 of May 30, 1974 (39 FR 19443) amended section 1 by deleting the reference to the section 5 authority and the numeral (2), and Executive Order 11867 section 6 of June 19, 1975 (40 FR 26253) revised section 1 to read as a designation of the Director for the authority of the President under section 500(a) of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (87 Stat. 390, 29 U.S.C. 790) with respect to the transfer of unexpended appropriations. Under the owner ruling on strike-and-insert amendments the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends; the restatement by Executive Order 11867 narrows section 1 to the section 500(a) authority and is a change of substance for the reviewer. The section 5 joint funding authority left the clause (it was delegated to the Administrator of General Services by Executive Order 11784 and Executive Order 11867, held as actor texts), which is a partial change, not an end of the clause. No held source shows that section 500(a) of the Rehabilitation Act or the Director's designation ended, so the amended clause is operative on 2026-10-14; the text of 29 U.S.C. 790 is not held and that limit is stated.

research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search. EO 11758 (signed 1974-01-15; 39 FR 2075; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11758.txt, read in full) delegates presidential authority under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget and the Secretary of Labor, authorizes agency heads to exempt contracts from section 503, and requires procurement regulations to carry a section 503 compliance provision. Identity: the heading of Executive Order 11758 delegating authority of the President under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 at 39 FR 2075, the title and the date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory held section 1 and one run covering sections 2, 3 and 4, so I replaced it with four clauses (inventory override): sections 1, 2, 3 and 4. Own terms: no section has an end date or ending condition; sections 1 and 4 were amended by later orders held as actor texts (EO 11784, EO 11867 and EO 12608), recorded as later events, and none of them revokes the order or any section. Later instruments: a search of every held order text for the number 11758 finds EO 11784 (amends section 1), EO 11867 (revises section 1), EO 12608 (amends section 4), the order's own Federal Register copy, the 1989 codification snapshot and Federal Register rules that cite it as authority; EO 11784 and EO 11867 are the amendments of section 1 and EO 12608 the amendment of section 4, each attached to its clause as a later event with its effective date. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record 9, 9 and 6 hits for the order number respectively. Limit stated plainly: the continuing predicate rests on the held original text, the held later amendments and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09); the text of 29 U.S.C. 790 and of section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act as now codified is not held, and the held rules citing the order are leads that its sections 2 to 4 continue, not quoted because they are not packet sources.
